items.title: validate_uri lets Azure (168.63.129.16) and Alibaba (100.100.100.200) metadata endpoints through
items.body:
`validate_uri` blocks cloud metadata endpoints as a side effect of the private-range check, so the two that sit on publicly-routable IPs go straight through.

`bytes_from` reaches `urlopen` for anything `validate_uri` lets past, and `src` there is model- or user-supplied (`image("https://...")`, `audio(...)`).

Ran every metadata endpoint I could name through `validate_uri` on `main` @ 21b1d90:

| endpoint | `allow_private=False` (default) | `is_private` / `is_link_local` / `is_reserved` | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `169.254.169.254` | blocked | True / True / False | AWS, GCP, Azure, OCI, DigitalOcean IMDS |
| `169.254.170.2` | blocked | True / True / False | AWS ECS task IAM role credentials |
| `169.254.170.23` | blocked | True / True / False | AWS EKS Pod Identity Agent |
| `169.254.42.42` | blocked | True / True / False | Scaleway |
| `192.0.0.192` | blocked | True / False / False | Oracle Cloud (Classic) |
| **`168.63.129.16`** | **ALLOWED** | False / False / False | Azure WireServer / platform channel |
| **`100.100.100.200`** | **ALLOWED** | False / False / False | Alibaba Cloud |

```python
from guidance._uri_validation import validate_uri
validate_uri("https://168.63.129.16/machine/")   # returns, no exception
validate_uri("https://100.100.100.200/latest/meta-data/")  # returns, no exception
```

`168.63.129.16` is a real public address Microsoft routes to the host agent on every Azure VM; `100.100.100.200` is in `100.64.0.0/10`, which Python does not report as private. Neither is covered by `is_private`/`is_link_local`/`is_reserved`, so nothing in `_check_ip_address` sees them.

Second, `allow_private=True` skips `_validate_hostname_not_private` entirely, so on that path all seven rows above become reachable — including `169.254.169.254`. `allow_private` reads like "let me hit my own LAN", and reaching IMDS is a different thing from reaching a host on your subnet. An explicit metadata denylist checked before the `allow_private` branch would keep those separate.

The IP-literal handling is otherwise thorough — `::ffff:127.0.0.1`, `0:0:0:0:0:ffff:a9fe:a9fe`, `64:ff9b::169.254.169.254` and `2002:a9fe:a9fe::` are all blocked, and `getaddrinfo` covering every A record closes the multi-record case.

Redirect revalidation is #1464, separate from this — the addresses above are rejected or accepted on the first hop, before any redirect is involved.

Environment: `guidance` @ 21b1d90, Python 3.10.12.
